inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash-flow add-back 'Equity-based compensation' $83.6M plus $26.1M taxes paid on net-share settlement of equity awards (financing activities). CDW publishes no combined figure (its non-GAAP line is expense plus associated payroll taxes, not withholding), so the two lines are summed. 9M-2026: $76.9M expense + $12.9M award taxes.
inputs.share_count_basis: 125.0M shares outstanding at 2026-09-30 (Q3-2026 10-Q balance sheet) plus ~0.6M treasury-method dilution (Q3 diluted 125.7M vs basic 125.1M) = 125.6M fully diluted. Already includes the restricted stock issued as part-consideration for Lovelytics (non-SBC issuance, ~0.3M shares, so no forward issuance is modelled). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows. CDW is a repurchaser ($653M FY2025, $652.7M 9M-2026), so the flat count is funded, not a convention.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free ~4.2% (10y UST), beta ~1.05, ERP 5.0% -> cost of equity ~9.5%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~5.8% (new notes 5.70-6.35%; legacy notes lower) -> ~4.4% after tax. Market-value weights ~74% equity ($19.7bn) / 26% debt ($7.1bn) -> ~8.2%; rounded up to 8.5% for the AI-hardware cyclicality in the near-term revenue. Same WACC in every scenario: risk is carried in the scenario paths and weights, not a WACC premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases: lease cost sits inside selling & administrative expense, so EBITDA is already post-rent; operating lease liabilities ($143.1M non-current + current portion) are NOT in net debt. One treatment, applied once. Leases are immaterial (~0.6% of EV).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing row 'operating company'). CDW is a US IT value-added reseller/integrator -- an operating company with FCF; no bank, REIT or holdco features, no prior valuation or memory entry. FY0 CHOICE: FY0 is FY2026E, not FY2025, because the balance sheet anchor is 2026-09-30: projecting FY2026 as year 1 from a Sep-2026 net-debt figure would count nine months of FY2026 cash flow twice. FY2026E revenue $25,250M = 9M actual $19,006.5M + Q4 estimate ~$6,240M (Q4-2025 $5,510.6M +13%, consistent with 9M growth of +12.4% and management's 'orders outpacing invoicing, backlog building' at Q3). FY2026E EBITDA pre-SBC ~8.6% = GAAP operating income ~$1,764M (9M $1,294.1M + Q4 ~$470M) + D&A ~$305M + SBC ~$104M. GAAP operating income (not non-GAAP) is used so recurring transformation/integration costs stay in; acquisition intangible amortization stays in D&A (non-cash, added back). Historic EBITDA-pre-SBC margin: FY2022 8.9%, FY2023 9.6%, FY2024 9.5%, FY2025 9.1%, FY2026E 8.6% (AI server/storage mix compressed gross margin to 20.5% in Q3-2026 from 21.9%). Working capital: distributor with receivables + inventory > payables, so wc_capture is NEGATIVE (growth consumes cash); net working capital ~8-9% of revenue, DSO lengthening (100 days vs 92). Year-1 component check: base FY2027 owner FCF ~$1.46bn (5.4% of revenue) vs FY2025 unlevered owner FCF ~$1.24bn (reported FCF $1,088M + after-tax interest ~$176M - award taxes $26M) on $22.4bn revenue (5.5%), so no one-off is carried forward. TTM-to-Q3-2026 reported FCF is only ~$934M because inventory (AI project build, product financing arrangement) and receivables rose; treated as timing, partly captured by the negative wc_capture. Inventory financing payable ($599M) treated as trade working capital, not debt, matching CDW's own definition of net debt. The $1,009M 2.670% notes due Dec-2026 will be repaid from the cash already held, so net debt is unaffected. Interest income is not stripped: CDW is net-debt.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (15-18%) diverges by far more than 30% from revenue (-1.9%/4.0%) and EPS (-0.4%/8.0%). Book equity is a small residual of the 2007 LBO deficit plus ~$0.5-1.5bn/yr of buybacks, so its growth says nothing about the business; revenue 5yr CAGR is used instead.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - equity-award taxes): FY2020 $1,091M, FY2022 $1,094M, FY2025 $978M. Owner FCF CAGR is ~1pp below reported, i.e. SBC plus award taxes have grown faster than cash flow, though the absolute charge is small (~0.5% of revenue). FY2022 was the post-COVID hardware peak; FY2023-24 a digestion trough; FY2026 an AI-infrastructure upcycle (+12% revenue 9M).

base.narrative: AI infrastructure backlog carries FY2027 to +6%, then growth settles to the ~4% long-run pace (IT spend modestly above GDP plus share gains from a fragmented VAR market and tuck-ins like Lovelytics). Gross margin recovers only partly: EBITDA-pre-SBC margin rebuilds from 8.6% to 8.8%, below the 9.5% of FY2023-24, as services mix offsets lower-margin server/storage.

bull.narrative: Enterprise AI capex is a multi-year build, not a one-year bulge: the backlog converts to +11% in FY2027 and the PC refresh plus sovereign/public-sector AI projects keep growth above 5% through FY2031. Services (Mission Cloud, Lovelytics, Digital Velocity) grow into a materially larger share, restoring margin to ~9.3% -- near the FY2023-24 level -- and CDW keeps consolidating share from smaller VARs.

bear.narrative: FY2026 was an AI pull-forward like FY2021-22: server/storage demand digests, revenue falls 4% in FY2027 and is flat in FY2028 (the FY2023-24 pattern, when revenue fell 10% then 2%). Margin does not recover because OEMs and hyperscaler marketplaces (AWS/Azure/Google) take more transactional volume direct and the remaining mix stays hardware-heavy; EBITDA-pre-SBC margin settles at 8.1%. Government/education budget pressure and the open DOJ E-Rate False Claims Act inquiry weigh on the public book. Leverage (net debt ~2.6x EBITDA) constrains buybacks but is not a solvency risk.

scenario_narratives.base: AI infrastructure backlog carries FY2027 to +6%, then ~4% long-run growth from IT spend above GDP, share gains and tuck-in services M&A; EBITDA-pre-SBC margin rebuilds only to 8.8% (from 8.6% FY2026E, vs 9.5% FY2023-24) as services offset lower-margin AI hardware mix.
scenario_narratives.bull: AI capex is a multi-year enterprise build plus a PC refresh: +11% FY2027, >5% growth into FY2031; services (Mission Cloud, Lovelytics) scale and margin returns to ~9.3%; continued share consolidation from smaller VARs.
scenario_narratives.bear: FY2026 was a pull-forward: a FY2023-style digestion (-4% FY2027, flat FY2028), OEM-direct and hyperscaler-marketplace disintermediation keep margin at 8.1%, public-sector budget and DOJ E-Rate risk weigh on the government/education book.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 25% from the 15% default because CDW's revenue is cyclical hardware and FY2026's growth rests on AI server/storage demand that has a clear precedent of digestion (FY2022 peak -> FY2023 -10%). Base 50% as the central path. Bull cut to 25% because it needs both a multi-year AI build AND a margin recovery against an adverse mix -- two independent things going right.

valuation_philosophy.summary: CDW is a capital-light, high-ROIC distributor whose value rests on a thin but durable ~8.5-9% EBITDA margin on a large, slowly-growing revenue base. The valuation is driven by margin (each 0.1pp of EBITDA margin is ~$25M of EBITDA) and by whether the 2026 AI hardware surge is durable or a pull-forward. Owner FCF charges SBC and award-withholding taxes (~0.5% of revenue, small) and a negative working-capital capture, since a distributor's growth consumes receivables and inventory.
key_risks_to_valuation: AI server/storage pull-forward reverses (FY2022->FY2023 precedent: -10% revenue)
Gross margin mix compression persists below 21% as hardware-heavy AI projects dominate
OEM-direct and hyperscaler-marketplace disintermediation of transactional resale
Leverage up to $7.1bn gross debt after Lovelytics and new notes at 5.7-6.35% coupons
Lengthening DSO (100 days) and inventory build consuming cash beyond the modelled capture
Open DOJ False Claims Act inquiry into E-Rate bidding (education/public book)
